purpose: Section 12: certify real-Postgres ingestion identity/dedup/concurrency semantics, independently reproducing and adversarially extending the P1-3 remediation reported in docs/phase-3f1-5-r-residual-foundation/10-onboarding-dedup-remediation.json.

environment.migrateStatus: Database schema is up to date!

baselineRegression.purpose: Re-run the PRIOR phase's own test files fresh, as a baseline, before adding independent adversarial tests.
baselineRegression.result: 11/11 tests PASS against real Postgres in this session.
baselineRegression.verdict: CONFIRMED - the prior phase's own reported P1-3 remediation is genuinely reproducible, not merely self-reported.

tests.name: AUDITOR TEST 1: 20-way genuinely concurrent upload race via Promise.all (not allSettled)
tests.detail: 20 simultaneous real uploadDocumentThroughIngestion calls for identical bytes/same tenant. Exactly 1 winner, 19 duplicates, 1 surviving Document/SourceArtifact row, zero unhandled rejections (Promise.all did not throw). Stricter than the prior phase's own N=10 allSettled test.

tests.name: AUDITOR TEST 2: mixed-entry-point concurrency (direct wrapper calls interleaved with the real uploadDocumentAction server action)
tests.detail: 5 direct uploadDocumentThroughIngestion calls + 5 real uploadDocumentAction calls, all fired via a single Promise.all, racing on identical bytes. Converged on exactly 1 Document/SourceArtifact regardless of which entry point 'won'.

tests.name: AUDITOR TEST 3: two real tenants uploading byte-identical content SIMULTANEOUSLY (concurrency + tenant isolation combined)
tests.detail: 5 concurrent uploads per tenant, both tenants racing at the same time. Each tenant converged to exactly 1 of its own rows; the two tenants' artifacts never merged despite an identical contentHash.

tests.name: AUDITOR TEST 4: 3-version supersedesDocumentId chain survives 5 concurrent duplicate re-uploads of the base document
tests.detail: A base->amendment1->amendment2 supersedesDocumentId chain was constructed, then the BASE document's exact bytes were re-uploaded 5 times concurrently. The chain (both supersedesDocumentId links) and the base row count (still exactly 1) were both completely undisturbed.

tests.name: AUDITOR TEST 5: metadata-only differences (renamed file, different declaredType) still dedup to the same document
tests.detail: Content, not filename/declaredType, is identity - confirmed independently.

concurrencyTestExactResults.summaryForCaller: 20-way Promise.all (not allSettled) concurrent real-Postgres uploads of identical bytes for the same tenant: exactly 1 winner (duplicate=false), exactly 19 losers (duplicate=true, all agreeing on the SAME artifactId as the winner), exactly 1 surviving Document row, exactly 1 surviving SourceArtifact row, ZERO unhandled promise rejections. Re-run 5+ times during this audit with identical results each time.

findings.title: lib/connectors/registry.ts's getOrCreateUploadConnection has its own, UNFIXED TOCTOU race - reliably reproducible, throws unhandled P2002 under concurrency
findings.discoveredBy: Independent auditor adversarial test (tests/foundation-audit/repro-connection-race.test.ts), not present in any prior phase's own test suite.
findings.description: uploadDocumentThroughIngestion's FIRST action on every call is `await getOrCreateUploadConnection(params.companyId)` (lib/connectors/upload-connector.ts:122), which does a Prisma `upsert` keyed on the (companyId, connectorType) unique constraint (lib/connectors/registry.ts:100-112). This upsert is NOT atomic against a concurrent identical-key upsert in this codebase's Prisma 5.22.0/Postgres setup: two or more concurrent FIRST calls for a brand-new company reliably race, and the losing caller(s) receive a raw, unhandled PrismaClientKnownRequestError (P2002) instead of the correct row - unlike uploadDocumentThroughIngestion's OWN artifact-creation step one line further down, which this same phase (P1-3 remediation) explicitly wrapped in a P2002 catch for exactly this race class. That fix was not applied here, one level up in the same call chain.

reproduction.method: 20 trials x 6 genuinely concurrent (Promise.allSettled) getOrCreateUploadConnection calls, each trial against a FRESH company (so every trial exercises the true first-ever-call race window)
reproduction.result: 96-100 of the 120 total concurrent calls (across repeated runs of this audit) threw an unhandled P2002 rejection. Reproduced on every run of this audit (5+ runs, ~80% rejection rate observed each time). Exactly 1 CompanySourceConnection row always survives per company - the unique constraint itself is never violated at the DB level - only the CALLER-facing behavior (a raw thrown error instead of a converged, successful result) is defective.
reproduction.testFile: tests/foundation-audit/repro-connection-race.test.ts (kept in the suite as `it.fails(...)` so the overall suite stays green while still serving as a live regression check - if a future fix resolves the race, this specific test will start failing, which is the correct signal to convert it to a normal assertion).

findings.impact: A company's very FIRST concurrent document upload attempt (e.g. a double-click submit, two browser tabs open to the onboarding Documents page, or two near-simultaneous onboarding actions before that company's DOCUMENT_UPLOAD connection row exists) can receive a raw 500-class error instead of succeeding. Once the connection row exists (after the first successful call for that company), this exact race window closes permanently for that company - ongoing/steady-state uploads are unaffected. No data corruption, no duplicate rows, and no cross-tenant leakage result from this - the defect is bounded to an unhandled-error path on a narrow, one-time-per-company timing window.
findings.whyNotBlocker: Does not corrupt data, does not create silent duplicates, does not leak cross-tenant, does not touch migrations or FK integrity - none of the ground rules' named BLOCKER archetypes apply. The blast radius is narrow (first-ever-upload timing window only) and the fix pattern (a P2002 catch + re-fetch, mirroring the SAME phase's own fix one line below in the same function) already exists as precedent elsewhere in this exact file.
findings.recommendedNextStep: Wrap getOrCreateUploadConnection's upsert in the same P2002-catch-and-refetch pattern uploadDocumentThroughIngestion's own artifact-creation step already uses, or make the upsert's own 'create' branch tolerant of a concurrent winner by re-querying on P2002.

findings.title: The prior phase's own concurrency test (tests/connectors/upload-connector.test.ts) never exercised the connection-creation race - a real test-coverage blind spot, now closed by this audit's own test
findings.description: That file's own 'getOrCreateUploadConnection is idempotent' test runs FIRST (creating the DOCUMENT_UPLOAD connection for the fixture company) and only AFTER that does its 10-way concurrent-duplicate-ingestion test run - so the connection row already exists by the time that concurrency test fires, and AUD-S12-01's race was never exercised. This audit's own tests/foundation-audit/ingestion-identity-certification.test.ts deliberately pre-warms both audit companies' connections in beforeAll for the SAME reason (to isolate content-identity/dedup certification from this separately-reported defect) - and tests/foundation-audit/repro-connection-race.test.ts exists specifically to close this coverage gap.
findings.recommendedNextStep: None required from this audit; noted for completeness.

certifiedClaims.identicalBytesSameTenantDeduplicate: CERTIFIED - reproduced independently, including under 20-way real concurrency.
certifiedClaims.alternateUploadEntryPathsConverge: CERTIFIED - direct wrapper call vs. real server action call, including when racing simultaneously, converge on one Document.
certifiedClaims.concurrencyDoesNotDuplicate: CERTIFIED for the content-identity/dedup mechanism itself (SourceArtifact's @@unique([companyId, contentHash]) + its P2002 catch). NOT fully certified end-to-end for a brand-new company's very first concurrent upload, due to AUD-S12-01 (a separate, one-level-up dependency's own unfixed race) - see finding for scope and severity.
certifiedClaims.differentTenantsRemainIsolated: CERTIFIED - byte-identical content across two tenants, including under simultaneous concurrent load, never merges.
certifiedClaims.intentionalHistoricalVersionsViaSupersed: CERTIFIED - a 3-version chain survives concurrent duplicate pressure on its base document untouched.

verdictNarrative: Every claim in the P1-3 remediation report was independently reproduced with fresh, adversarial constructions against real Postgres, including a stricter own concurrency test than the prior phase ran. No BLOCKER-class defect (no cross-tenant merge, no silent duplicate creation, no data corruption) was found anywhere in the content-identity/dedup mechanism itself. One MAJOR_NON_BLOCKING finding (AUD-S12-01) was independently discovered in a dependency this mechanism calls (the lazy CompanySourceConnection auto-creation), representing an unfixed instance of the exact same concurrency-race class this phase otherwise fixed one line further down in the same function.
